sources.citation: Keegan, John M. (n.d.). Sara-Bagirmi Language Project bibliography, 7 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliography only; lists Bongo & Fédry 1981 and Palayer 2006 (A&L 10). Keegan's own lexicons cover Kaba, Kaba Na and Kulfa, not Deme.

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 2013. Notes on the classification of Sara Kaba languages. Sara-Bagirmi Language Project, 3 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone; segmental differences Sara Kaba vs Sara Proper only. Quotes Deme forms from Palayer 2006:201, 204 (e/ɛ contrast), confirming Palayer 2006 is the primary phonological source for Deme.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal & Pierre Nougayrol. 2008. Les langues soudaniques centrales: essai d'évaluation. In M. Bechhaus-Gerst, D. Ibriszimow & R. Vossen (eds), Problems of Linguistic-Historical Reconstruction in Africa (SUGIA Beiheft 19), 9–29. Köln: Köppe. HAL halshs-00348133.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level only, Deme not named. Preprint p.6: 'Les langues SBB connaissent des systèmes à deux, trois ou quatre hauteurs tonales, dont les correspondances répondent à des formules spécifiques selon qu’on envisage noms ou verbes'; p.7: 'Le système tonal *SBB est caractérisé par deux tons distinctifs. Les langues occidentales (cf. infra) résultent toutes d’un système postérieur (*OCC) qui a développé un troisième ton vers le haut.' No mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (SIL Chad). 2007. Change Request 2007-193: Kaba Deme → Sara Kaba Démé [kwg] (adopted 2008-01-14).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; name-change form. Cites an April 2005 sociolinguistic survey and Bongo & Fédry 1981 as the only published source.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2006. Présentation des langues sara-bongo-baguirmiennes. Paris: CNRS-LLACAN, electronic document accompanying Boyeldieu, Nougayrol & Palayer 2006, Lexique comparatif historique des langues SBB. 24 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent (a full-text search for stress/accent → no relevant hit). Sources table p.3 lists 'sim sime (’dem nord) Palayer 2006' and 'dem ’dem (centre) Fédry (inédit)', i.e. Palayer 2006 describes the northern Deme variety (sime). Pp.10–11 define tonal correspondence formulas for SBB languages with 2, 3 or 4 tone registers; Sara languages have a three-register (*OCC) system.
